HELLO.name: Hello / Greetings
HELLO.meaning: Standard friendly greeting used to acknowledge someone and start a conversation.
HELLO.description: Open hand with fingers flat and held together, moving outward from near the temple or forehead in a welcoming salute.
HELLO.usage: Used at the start of any conversation in ASL. Typically accompanied by a warm smile and direct eye contact.
HELLO.example_sentence: Hello! It is wonderful to meet you today.
HELLO.confusable_with: Casual waving; ensure hand starts near forehead and moves outward smoothly.
hints: Open your hand completely with fingers straight and together.
Hold hand near eye level facing outward.
Keep wrist steady with a slight forward motion.
HELLO.fun_fact: In Deaf culture, greeting everyone in the room individually is a sign of deep respect.

THANK_YOU.name: Thank You / Gratitude
THANK_YOU.meaning: Universal expression of gratitude and appreciation.
THANK_YOU.description: Flat hand with fingertips touching lightly near lips or chin, then moving forward and slightly down toward the other person.
THANK_YOU.usage: Used whenever someone offers help, a compliment, or a gift. Moving the hand toward the recipient directs the gratitude.
THANK_YOU.example_sentence: Thank you so much for helping me practice!
THANK_YOU.confusable_with: Looks similar to 'GOOD', but 'GOOD' drops into the opposite open palm, whereas 'THANK YOU' stays airborne.
hints: Touch fingertips lightly near your chin.
Move hand gently forward toward the camera.
Face your palm toward yourself as you start.
THANK_YOU.fun_fact: The gesture originates from speech emerging from the lips with gratitude.

YES.name: Yes / Affirmation
YES.meaning: Affirmative answer signifying agreement, confirmation, or approval.
YES.description: Fist held in front of you, tilting up and down twice from the wrist like a head nodding yes.
YES.usage: Direct answer to questions, indicating consent or agreement in conversation.
YES.example_sentence: Yes, I understand and agree with your idea.
YES.confusable_with: A static fist; make sure to tilt the wrist forward in a nod.
hints: Make a solid fist with knuckles facing forward.
Nod the fist slightly at the wrist.
Maintain a pleasant, affirmative facial expression.
YES.fun_fact: The fist visually represents your head nodding up and down.

NO.name: No / Negative
NO.meaning: Clear refusal or denial signifying disagreement or negation.
NO.description: Index and middle fingers extended together, quickly snapping down onto the thumb tip like a closing beak.
NO.usage: Direct response to decline offers or deny questions. Often paired with a slight head shake.
NO.example_sentence: No, I do not mind at all.
NO.confusable_with: Letter 'O'; in 'NO', index and middle fingers snap down decisively.
hints: Keep ring and pinky fingers tucked into your palm.
Bring index and middle fingertips together onto thumb tip.
Snap fingers down decisively.
NO.fun_fact: Linguists trace this sign back to the letters N and O fingerspelled in rapid succession.

PLEASE.name: Please / Politeness
PLEASE.meaning: Polite request expressing courtesy and consideration.
PLEASE.description: Flat open hand with fingers together, placed over the center of the chest and moving in gentle clockwise circles.
PLEASE.usage: Used whenever making a request, asking for assistance, or showing good manners.
PLEASE.example_sentence: Please could you explain that one more time?
PLEASE.confusable_with: 'SORRY' (which uses a closed fist over chest; 'PLEASE' uses a flat open palm).
hints: Keep palm open and flat with fingers touching.
Hold hand against center of upper chest.
Make a gentle circular rubbing motion.
PLEASE.fun_fact: The circular chest motion symbolizes soothing and softening the heart.

SORRY.name: Sorry / Apology
SORRY.meaning: Expression of remorse, sympathy, or apology.
SORRY.description: Closed fist with thumb across fingers, rubbed in circular motions over the heart / chest area.
SORRY.usage: Used to apologize for an error or express empathy ('I am sorry for your loss').
SORRY.example_sentence: I am so sorry for arriving late to our meeting.
SORRY.confusable_with: 'PLEASE'; remember that 'SORRY' uses a closed fist, while 'PLEASE' uses an open palm.
hints: Make a firm fist with thumb wrapped across fingers.
Place knuckles against your upper chest.
Rub in a slow circular motion.
SORRY.fun_fact: Rubbing the fist over the chest symbolizes rubbing away sorrow from the heart.

HELP.name: Help / Assistance
HELP.meaning: Request for or offer of aid, support, or rescue.
HELP.description: Dominant hand makes an 'A' fist with thumb pointing up, resting atop the flat open palm of the other hand, lifted upward together.
HELP.usage: Critical emergency and cooperative sign. Directional: moving toward you means 'help me'; moving toward them means 'I help you'.
HELP.example_sentence: Can you please help me with this project?
HELP.confusable_with: Thumb-up gesture; in ASL, the supporting open palm beneath is essential.
hints: Make a thumbs-up handshape with your right hand.
Rest it firmly atop your open left palm.
Lift both hands upward together.
HELP.fun_fact: The bottom flat hand literally lifts up the other hand, symbolizing mutual support.

I_LOVE_YOU.name: I Love You (ILY)
I_LOVE_YOU.meaning: Deep affection, love, friendship, and warm wishes.
I_LOVE_YOU.description: Thumb, index finger, and pinky finger extended simultaneously. Middle and ring fingers folded flat into palm.
I_LOVE_YOU.usage: Known worldwide. Used among family, friends, loved ones, and at community gatherings to express solidarity and care.
I_LOVE_YOU.example_sentence: I love you and I am always here for you!
I_LOVE_YOU.confusable_with: The rock-and-roll horns (which tucks the thumb). 'I LOVE YOU' MUST have the thumb extended outward!
hints: Extend your thumb, index finger, and pinky finger all at once.
Keep middle and ring fingers curled firmly against your palm.
Hold palm facing forward toward the camera.
I_LOVE_YOU.fun_fact: The ILY sign combines the manual alphabet letters 'I', 'L', and 'Y' into one gesture.

GOOD.name: Good / Well
GOOD.meaning: Positive evaluation signifying quality, satisfaction, or wellbeing.
GOOD.description: Fingertips of dominant flat hand touch lips or chin, then move down into the open palm of the non-dominant hand.
GOOD.usage: Used in greetings ('Good morning'), answering 'How are you?' ('I am good'), and praising work ('Good job!').
GOOD.example_sentence: Everything is going very good today.
GOOD.confusable_with: 'THANK YOU'; 'GOOD' finishes by landing into the palm of the opposite hand.
hints: Flat open hand touches chin lightly.
Brings hand downward into open waiting palm.
Smile to emphasize positive feeling.
GOOD.fun_fact: One of the most frequently used adjectives in American Sign Language.

STOP.name: Stop / Halt
STOP.meaning: Instruction to halt an action, pause, or cease movement.
STOP.description: One hand held flat palm-up while the other hand chops down vertically with its outer edge into the palm.
STOP.usage: Clear directive command used in driving, sports, conversation, or asking someone to cease an action.
STOP.example_sentence: Please stop and listen for a moment.
STOP.confusable_with: Casual waving; the firm downward karate-chop motion is unmistakable.
hints: Keep hand straight with fingers glued together.
Deliver a firm, crisp downward motion.
Face palm perpendicular to the supporting hand.
STOP.fun_fact: The physical chopping contact conveys an immediate, unambiguous boundary.

OK.name: Okay / Approved
OK.meaning: Agreement, approval, or confirming that everything is satisfactory.
OK.description: Thumb and index fingertips meet to form a clean circular loop, while middle, ring, and pinky fingers fan upward.
OK.usage: Universally recognized sign for agreement, fine condition, or acknowledging instructions.
OK.example_sentence: Everything is completely okay, do not worry.
OK.confusable_with: Letter 'D' (where index is up and other three fingers form loop with thumb).
hints: Make a circle by touching the tips of your thumb and index finger.
Keep other three fingers straight and separated.
Hold hand stable at chest height.
OK.fun_fact: The circle represents the letter 'O' and the three upright fingers represent 'K'.

PEACE.name: Peace / Harmony
PEACE.meaning: Symbol of tranquility, unity, victory, and goodwill.
PEACE.description: Index and middle fingers extended straight up and separated into a wide 'V' shape, with other fingers curled down by thumb.
PEACE.usage: Global emblem of harmony, peaceful coexistence, and victory.
PEACE.example_sentence: Wishing peace and friendship to all people.
PEACE.confusable_with: Letter 'V' or number '2'; culturally identical posture.
hints: Extend index and middle fingers straight up.
Spread the two fingers wide apart into a V.
Lock down ring and pinky fingers with your thumb.
PEACE.fun_fact: Adopted by Deaf and hearing communities worldwide as a universal greeting of peace.

WELCOME.name: Welcome / Hospitality
WELCOME.meaning: Gracious invitation or reception extending warmth to guests.
WELCOME.description: Open hand with palm facing slightly up, swept from out in front of you smoothly toward your body.
WELCOME.usage: Used when receiving visitors ('Welcome to our home') or replying to 'Thank you' ('You are welcome').
WELCOME.example_sentence: You are always welcome in our community!
WELCOME.confusable_with: Beckoning; welcome is an open-palm gracious sweeping curve toward your body.
hints: Open hand in a welcoming, relaxed curve.
Start with hand forward at waist level.
Sweep hand gently inward toward your torso.
WELCOME.fun_fact: The motion visually draws the person into your personal space and warmth.

CALL_ME.name: Call Me / Phone
CALL_ME.meaning: Instruction or request to communicate via phone or video call.
CALL_ME.description: Thumb and pinky extended (Shaka sign / 'Y') held up to the ear like a phone receiver.
CALL_ME.usage: Modern conversational gesture meaning 'Call me later' or 'I will phone you'.
CALL_ME.example_sentence: Please call me when you arrive home safely.
CALL_ME.confusable_with: Letter 'Y'; 'CALL ME' brings the hand to the ear/side of face.
hints: Extend only your thumb and pinky finger outward.
Curl your index, middle, and ring fingers tightly.
Tilt thumb toward ear and pinky toward mouth.
CALL_ME.fun_fact: A universal visual metaphor representing an old-fashioned telephone handset.

WATER.name: Water / Refreshment
WATER.meaning: Essential liquid for hydration, drinking, and life.
WATER.description: 'W' handshape (index, middle, ring fingers extended upright) tapped gently twice against the chin.
WATER.usage: Common everyday sign when asking for a drink or talking about hydration.
WATER.example_sentence: May I please have a glass of water?
WATER.confusable_with: Letter 'W'; 'WATER' specifically taps the index finger against the chin twice.
hints: Form the letter 'W' with index, middle, and ring fingers up.
Hold down your pinky with your thumb.
Tap your index finger twice gently against your chin.
WATER.fun_fact: Initialized from the English letter W, placed near the mouth where water is consumed.
